test_title: SSC CGL Tier-II (AAO) 2023 Official Paper-III (Held On: 27 Oct, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In relation to the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003, '_______' means the gross domestic product reckoned at constant prices, as published by the Central Statistics Office from time to time.
solution:
The correct answer is** Real gross domestic product**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Real gross domestic product:**

 
 
• Real gross domestic product (GDP) is the measure of a country's economic output adjusted for price changes (inflation or deflation). It reflects the value of all goods and services produced by an economy at constant prices, providing a more accurate representation of economic performance over time.
 
• In the context of the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003, using real GDP allows for a consistent comparison of economic data by removing the effects of price level changes.
 
• Real GDP is published by the Central Statistics Office (CSO) and serves as a crucial metric for policymakers to design and implement fiscal policies aimed at sustainable economic growth.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Notional gross domestic product:**

 
 
• This term is not commonly used in economic analysis. The correct term is nominal GDP, which measures a country's economic output using current prices, without adjusting for inflation. Nominal GDP can be misleading for long-term comparisons due to price level changes.
 
 
 
• **Secondary gross domestic product:**
 
 
• This is not a recognized economic term. GDP is generally categorized into primary, secondary, and tertiary sectors, but there is no specific measure called secondary GDP.
 
 
 
• **Residual gross domestic product:**
 
 
• This term does not exist in standard economic terminology. Residuals in economic models usually refer to the unexplained portion of a regression model, not a type of GDP measurement.
